name: Anzens USDA
oneLiner: USDA is Anzens' U.S.-MSB-licensed dollar stablecoin on Cardano, redeemable 1:1 against USD cash and Treasuries custodied by BitGo Trust.
collateral: USD and dollar-equivalent reserves including U.S. Treasuries, held in segregated accounts custodied by BitGo Trust (Qualified Custodian)
pegMechanism: Direct 1:1 USD redemption through Anzens via KYC-verified bank transfers; minting and burning available to retail and institutional users in eligible U.S. states

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Anzens' current terms and EMURGO's launch announcement describe a fully reserved, Cardano-native USDA issued through the Anzens portal with issuer-operated mint and burn flows, establishing the fiat-cash archetype.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDA is an Anzens-issued U.S. dollar stablecoin designed for mint, burn, send, receive, and off-ramp payment flows.

genius.licensingRegulator: FinCEN MSB / 17 US state no-objection letters; BitGo Trust qualified custodian
genius.notes: Anzens describes USDA as 100% backed and issued by Anzens Inc. (FinCEN MSB, 17 state no-objection letters), with reserves held at BitGo Trust. Pharos found no GENIUS PPSI approval, state-qualified approval, official application, or public intent statement. A LinkedIn post from EMURGO (2026) references a first proof-of-reserves examination report, but no dedicated reserve attestation or transparency URL is published on anzens.com or findable from public sources; reserveDisclosurePresent corrected to false. USDA relaunched under Encryptus partnership after a 2023 pause.

controls.evidence: Anzens mints/burns USDA 1:1 against segregated USD reserves and Treasuries custodied at BitGo Trust, gated by KYC bank transfers; no permissionless or user-collateralized mint route exists on the Cardano native policy.

review.evidence: Anzens (FinCEN MSB) is the sole issuer of USDA on Cardano; mint/redeem is centralized 1:1 via KYC bank transfers against BitGo Trust-custodied reserves. Policy ID fe7c786ab321f41c654ef6c1af7b3250a613c24e4213e0425a7ae456 confirmed via Koios as a PlutusV2 script (type=plutusV2, 154 mints / 123 burns confirmed, policy_asset_list verified). Minting transactions include uid metadata but no required_signers field is exposed in Koios tx_info; the PlutusV2 script validates internally with signing key(s) embedded as script parameters — not observable from chain state without full script parameter decoding. 2026-07-20 (Kimi P2 dc-2): Koios script_info confirms the minting policy is a plutusV2 script created in tx 77f120599d05ed304970bb9bda15f2a8f56aa6495178065444c601f0212e675a with the USDA asset name embedded; Anzens/EMURGO publish only custody-adjacent statements (EMURGO key-management blog; BitGo custodial services for USDA mint/burn operations) and no script parameterization, so the controlling signing keys remain unestablished from public sources. Re-reviewed 2026-07-27 (Kimi data review): anzens.com and Anzens/EMURGO channels still publish no script parameterization, admin-control inventory, or reserve attestation URL, so the review is complete to the extent public sources allow and is marked scoreable with confidence capped at manual-review; the controlling signing keys embedded as PlutusV2 script parameters remain the recorded structural unknown. Reconciliation is recorded as periodic: EMURGO announced an independent examination of USDA reserve assets (first proof-of-reserves report), which is a point-in-time supply-vs-reserve reconciliation engagement rather than a continuous feed; no attestation URL is publicly published.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-4 (lead usdf-falcon)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Anzens states that USDA reserves are held in segregated accounts custodied by BitGo Trust, a qualified custodian, which implies trust-style segregation and bankruptcy remoteness of client assets. The reviewed sources do not publish account-level terms, whether any reserve share sits outside BitGo Trust, or explicit rehypothecation prohibitions.
